1:
\textbf{(a)} Divide: $\dfrac{6x+5}{2x+1}=3+\dfrac{2}{2x+1}$. So
\[\int_0^4\Big(3+\frac{2}{2x+1}\Big)dx=\Big[3x+\ln|2x+1|\Big]_0^4=12+\ln9=\boxed{12+2\ln3}.\]
\textbf{(b)} $x^{3/2}+x^{1/2}=\sqrt x\,(x+1)$. Let $u=\sqrt x$, $dx=2u\,du$; $x=1\to u=1$, $x=3\to u=\sqrt3$:
\[\int_1^{\sqrt3}\frac{2u\,du}{u(u^2+1)}=2\Big[\tan^{-1}u\Big]_1^{\sqrt3}=2\Big(\frac\pi3-\frac\pi4\Big)=\boxed{\frac{\pi}{6}}.\]
2:
\textbf{(a)} Let $x=\sec\theta$ ($0<\theta<\frac\pi2$), $dx=\sec\theta\tan\theta\,d\theta$, $(x^2-1)^{3/2}=\tan^3\theta$:
\[\int\frac{\sec\theta\tan\theta}{\sec\theta\tan^3\theta}d\theta=\int\cot^2\theta\,d\theta=\int(\csc^2\theta-1)\,d\theta=-\cot\theta-\theta+C.\]
With $\cot\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}$:
\[\boxed{-\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}-\sec^{-1}x+C}.\]
\textbf{(b)} By parts with $u=\tan^{-1}x$, $dv=x^{-2}dx$ ($du=\frac{dx}{1+x^2}$, $v=-\frac1x$):
\[-\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{x}+\int\frac{dx}{x(1+x^2)}.\]
Partial fractions: $\frac{1}{x(1+x^2)}=\frac1x-\frac{x}{1+x^2}$. So
\[\boxed{-\frac{\tan^{-1}x}{x}+\ln|x|-\tfrac12\ln(1+x^2)+C}.\]
3:
\textbf{(a)}
\[\int_1^\infty x^{-3/2}dx=\lim_{t\to\infty}\Big[-2x^{-1/2}\Big]_1^t=\lim_{t\to\infty}\Big(2-\frac{2}{\sqrt t}\Big)=2.\]
The area is finite: \boxed{2}.

\textbf{(b)} Shells about the $y$-axis:
\[V=\int_1^\infty2\pi x\cdot x^{-3/2}dx=2\pi\lim_{t\to\infty}\Big[2\sqrt x\Big]_1^t=\infty.\]
The volume is \boxed{\text{infinite}} (the integral diverges).
4:
At 0.5 m/s the bucket reaches 8 m after 16 s; at height $y$ the time is $t=2y$. Water left at that moment: $25-0.3(2y)=25-0.6y$ liters $=25-0.6y$ kg. Force (weight) $9.8(25-0.6y)$ N. Work:
\[W=\int_0^8 9.8(25-0.6y)\,dy=9.8\Big[25y-0.3y^2\Big]_0^8=9.8(200-19.2)=\boxed{1771.84\ \text{J}}.\]
7:
\textbf{(a)} A shell at $x$ ($0\le x\le4$) has radius $6-x$ and height $\sqrt x$:
\[V=\int_0^42\pi(6-x)\sqrt x\,dx=2\pi\Big[4x^{3/2}-\tfrac25x^{5/2}\Big]_0^4=2\pi\Big(32-\frac{64}{5}\Big)=\boxed{\frac{192\pi}{5}}.\]
\textbf{(b)} Slice horizontally, $0\le y\le2$: the region runs from $x=y^2$ to $x=4$, so the outer radius is $6-y^2$ and the inner radius is $6-4=2$:
\[V=\int_0^2\pi\Big[(6-y^2)^2-2^2\Big]dy.\]
(It also equals $\frac{192\pi}{5}$.)
10:
\textbf{(a)} Newton's law: $T(t)=4+(T_0-4)e^{-kt}=4-14e^{-kt}$. $T(4)=-6$: $14e^{-4k}=10\Rightarrow k=\frac{\ln1.4}{4}\approx0.08412$:
\[\boxed{T(t)=4-14e^{-0.08412t}}\quad\Big(=4-14\,(5/7)^{t/4}\Big).\]
\textbf{(b)} $T=2$: $14e^{-kt}=2\Rightarrow t=\frac{\ln7}{k}=\frac{4\ln7}{\ln1.4}\approx23.13$ h. After the first 4 hours, you wait another \boxed{19.13\ \text{hours}}.
